correctness.rationale: Binary digit recurrence epsilon(2n+r)=(-1)^r epsilon(n) gives an explicit 9x9 integer matrix B on F_j(k). Independently multiplying shows B^6=3I+8Q-3J with Q_{ij}=1 iff i=j mod3, Q^2=3Q. For k>=1 the total of nine residue sums equals sum_{n<9*2^k}epsilon(n)=0, so JV(k)=0. The projector P=Q/3 yields V(k+6m)=3^m(I-P)V(k)+27^mPV(k), all k>=1,m>=0; V(1) has both components nonzero, so the vector order-two recurrence is minimal. Direct computations for all j, k=1..7, m=0..2 corroborate exact algebra but do not prove infinite cutoffs.
residual_risks: The sum k>=1 restriction is essential: JV(0) need not vanish, and no nondyadic conclusion follows.
